decisions.reason: SOL keeps the source's confident tone in natural English.
SOL preserves the public's intense enthusiasm and envy with idiomatic phrasing.
SOL keeps the comparison of childhood aspirations while using natural English list phrasing.
SOL preserves the sense that wealth and fame are the concepts associated with Hunters.

The Korean's 캐릭터 is a fresh public character or persona, not specifically a personality.
SOL changes an already heated voice that continues into one that grows progressively more heated.
SOL naturally preserves the image of the public heating up and cooling off even faster.
SOL drops the explicit reference to becoming a star from 반짝스타.
SOL naturally renders him briefly closing his mouth as falling silent.
SOL keeps the speaker's casual resolve in “might as well make things clear.”
SOL naturally expresses the same objection to being recruited.
The Korean describes the visible action of being about to speak; SOL changes it into an internal desire.
SOL makes the proposed agency arrangement explicit without changing the offer.
대주주 means a major shareholder, not necessarily a majority shareholder; SOL changes the ownership quantity.
SOL naturally clarifies that non-Guild professional work is permitted while preserving the legal contrast.
SOL keeps the sense that high-ranking Hunters commonly sign with entertainment or management agencies.
The Korean presents his misunderstanding as apparent to Won; SOL changes that observation into the speaker's opinion.
SOL preserves the conditional rebuttal and Taekyung's lack of desire to become a star.
SOL keeps the quantities and financial exaggeration while sounding more conversational.
The Korean explicitly says he spread both arms; SOL drops that physical detail.
SOL adds “years ago,” an unsupported temporal specification.

SOL adds “details,” narrowing an intentionally unspecified reference to what changed.
SOL preserves the same mutual action and presents it in natural English order.
SOL keeps the safer, faster agency route and the studio-versus-Gate contrast in fluent dialogue.
SOL drops both the bright smile and the explicit action of delivering lines in front of the camera.
“The physical type” naturally conveys someone who prefers using his body.
The Korean says his swearing would fail broadcast standards; SOL incorrectly makes Taekyung himself the subject.
The Korean depicts obvious existing bewilderment; SOL adds an unsupported progression in which it deepens.
SOL weakens the explicit claim that he can become a building owner without television or commercials.
SOL preserves the concession about A-rank income and the contrast with Gangnam land prices.
SOL is a natural equivalent of asking whether he knows the current price per pyeong there.
The Korean says he blinked; SOL changes that physical action into staring.
SOL makes the implied object explicit without changing the intended purchase.
SOL correctly renders 동네 상가 as a neighborhood commercial building.
SOL keeps the same commercial-building reference in natural English.
SOL changes Mom saying she is bored into simply becoming bored, dropping the source's speech cue.
SOL preserves the increasingly twisted facial reaction in more idiomatic prose.
SOL keeps the present result of his changed income while preserving the comparison with his past.
“No debt” is the natural English mass-noun rendering of the same financial state.
SOL preserves the narrator's clipped rhetorical distinction between attention and fame.
SOL naturally conveys the emphasis of 특히 while preserving the spotlight's exhausting unpleasantness.
SOL keeps the same family-centered realization in idiomatic English.
SOL preserves the pile of offers, selecting a few, filming them, and returning focus to the Guild.
SOL keeps the point that he can earn plenty without entering entertainment work.
SOL retains the long silence and delayed response without awkward literal phrasing.
SOL preserves the phone and caller identification while sounding more conversational.
SOL keeps the elapsed-time realization in natural narrative prose.
The Korean specifically says he received the number today and will contact him; SOL drops “today” and narrows contact to a call.
SOL preserves the invitation and promised song practice with natural word order.
SOL naturally clarifies that he expects Won to perform the original song live.
SOL preserves Won's faintly smiling nod as Taekyung leaves.
SOL is a natural polite offer to clear the cup.
SOL preserves the unanswered question, empty cup, and abrupt speech in smooth English.
SOL drops the softening hedge in 혹시, making the question more blunt than the source.
“Of course I have” naturally conveys the worker's acknowledgment that he knows Won.
SOL keeps the worker's unexpectedly high estimate of Won's fame and the limited childhood memories.
SOL restores the source's dry-as-sand image, which was absent from BASE.
Together with H060, SOL preserves the voice-triggered disappearance of the worker's smile without awkward repetition.
SOL preserves the worker's nervous observation, quiet return, elapsed time, and melody.
The source identifies the music as his own; SOL unnecessarily narrows it to one of several songs.
SOL's “all of it” naturally refers back to the song and preserves the past-relic image without overextending the referent.
BASE and SOL both lose the Korean rhetorical “who is that bastard making fun of?” structure; this preserves the target and indignation.
decisions.replacement: “Who does that bastard think he’s mocking…?”
